payload.title: Hero Rising
payload.blurb: Japan, the present day, where eight people in ten are born with a Quirk, a power that is theirs alone. Three weeks ago the League of Villains broke into a hero agency in Hosu and walked out again, and UA, the national hero school, has moved its first-years into a new dorm on campus where they can…
payload.overview: Japan, in a present where about eighty percent of people have a Quirk. Quirks run from useful to strange to nearly useless, and some shape the body: scales, extra arms, an animal's head. Only licensed heroes may use a Quirk to fight crime or rescue anyone, and most main streets keep a hero agency office every few blocks. Heroes are ranked each year on rescues, arrests and public votes, and the top ten are on television most weeks. All Might has been number one for thirty years and is called the Symbol of Peace. Musutafu is a coastal city of shopping streets, train lines and harbor cranes, with the UA campus on a hill above it. UA takes first-years by an entrance exam it grades without mercy, most of them fifteen or sixteen and a few older, passed on a later try, and it expels the ones it thinks will not survive the job. The League of Villains is a loose network that calls hero licensing a cage; it has struck agencies before, and it is patient. About one person in five is quirkless. Money is yen, the trains run on time, and the news is always on. There are no levels, classes or status windows here.
payload.intro:
Twenty to seven, your first morning in Heights Alliance. The building is quiet except for the kitchen tap you have just turned off. At the end of the ground-floor corridor the back door stands a hand's width open. Cold air comes through the gap with a smell like a struck match, and the steel latch plate is black and buckled, burned from this side.

Shota Aizawa is crouched in front of it in a black jumpsuit, a long grey scarf wound twice around his neck, his hair flat on one side from sleeping somewhere that was not a bed. He touches the latch with one finger and looks at the soot it leaves.

"The sensor says this opened at four and never shut," he says, without turning round. Then he does turn, and looks at you with red-rimmed eyes. "You're up early. Where were you at four?"
starters:
Ground Gamma is a mock city block of concrete shells and steel pipe, and Class 1-A stands in a ragged line along the white start mark in gym kit that still has the folds in it. Shota Aizawa sits on an upturned crate twenty meters off with a clipboard and a stopwatch. He has told you the rules once: one lap of the block, any Quirk, any route, and the lowest score of the morning goes to the principal's desk with a letter.

Katsuki Bakugo has taken the place beside you. His hands are pushed deep in his pockets, and when he takes them out the palms are pink and new, like skin that grew back overnight. He sees you looking.

"You're in my lane," he says. "Move, or keep up." Aizawa lifts the stopwatch.

The infirmary smells of antiseptic and the wrapped sweets in a bowl by the door. Your right wrist has swollen since Ground Gamma, hot and stiff, and Chiyo Shuzenji has it in both her small hands, turning it a little to see where you wince. On the next bed Izuku Midoriya lies with two fingers splinted, a notebook open on his chest that he cannot hold a pen for, watching the ceiling as if it had a problem on it.

Recovery Girl lets go of your wrist and holds up a roll of white tape in one hand. "Tape, and it aches for a week. Or I heal it now, and you sleep through the afternoon and miss English." She waits, lips already pursed.

"Take the tape," Midoriya says quietly, and then goes red. "Sorry. She's done four of us already."

Shiomi Street runs downhill from the back of Musutafu station under a covered roof of yellowed plastic, and most of its shutters are down by seven. Dobashi Noodles is still lit. Steam rolls out under the curtain, and inside there are eight stools at one counter, a television showing the Hosu footage again with the sound off, and one other customer: a man in a grey work jacket at the far end, eating slowly.

Hatsue Dobashi wipes down the counter in front of you and leans on it so her back is to him.

"Don't turn round," she says, low. "That one's eaten here every night for two weeks, and twice tonight he's asked me which of you UA first-years come in on your own." She puts down a pair of chopsticks. "You came in on your own."

entries.title: Your start
entries.content: You are 18, a first-year at UA in Class 1-A, one of twenty who passed this spring's entrance exam. You came to Musutafu alone, you have no family here, and a scholarship pays for the dorm. You carried your box into Heights Alliance last night. UA takes first-years from all over Japan, most of them fifteen or sixteen, and the twenty of you met for the first time at the exam, if at all.

entries.title: Factions
entries.content:
UA - the national hero school in Musutafu, which wants its first-years licensed, alive and seen to be safe.
Hero Public Safety Commission - the government office that licenses heroes, which wants no scandal and will close a dorm to avoid one.
League of Villains - a loose network that calls licensing a cage, which wants the hero system broken and first-years who will listen.
Hero agencies - licensed firms that patrol for contracts, which want their rankings up and the best first-years signed early.
Shiomi Street shopkeepers - the quirkless families of the old shopping street, who want the agencies to notice them and the League to leave.

entries.title: Quirks and the law
entries.content: About eight people in ten have a Quirk, a power that is theirs alone, from useful to strange to nearly useless. Only licensed heroes may use a Quirk to fight, chase or rescue anyone; for everyone else, using one on another person is a crime. Licenses come from the Hero Public Safety Commission after years at a hero school.

entries.title: UA and Class 1-A
entries.content: UA, on its hill above Musutafu, is the national hero school. It takes first-years, mostly fifteen or sixteen, by an entrance exam most applicants fail, and a few are older after a second try. Class 1-A holds twenty of them, and they have just moved into the new Heights Alliance dorm on campus. Any first-year can be expelled, and the staff do it.

entries.title: Musutafu
entries.content: Musutafu is a coastal city of shopping streets, train lines and high-rise flats. Musutafu station is the hub, and behind it Shiomi Street runs down to the harbor and its cargo cranes. Agency offices fill the glass district on the north bank. The UA campus sits on the hill above it all, twenty minutes' walk from the station.

entries.title: The UA campus
entries.content: UA's campus is white towers and steel fences on the hill above Musutafu. The main building holds the classrooms and the staff office, with the infirmary beside it. Beyond lie the training grounds, mock city blocks called Ground Beta and Ground Gamma. Heights Alliance stands at the north edge, the newest building on the hill.

entries.title: Heights Alliance
entries.content: Heights Alliance is the first-year dorm, opened this spring because of Hosu: four floors, a shared kitchen and common room on the ground floor, a wall screen always on the news. Each first-year has a room with a bed, a desk and a window. Every door locks on a sensor that logs each opening. Curfew is ten.

entries.title: The back door
entries.content: On the first morning in Heights Alliance the back door at the end of the ground-floor corridor was found burned open, its steel latch melted from the inside. The sensor logged it opening at four and never closing. Most of the class assume the League. The staff have not said what they think.

entries.title: Class 1-A
entries.content: Class 1-A is twenty first-years who met at the exam, if at all. Among them: Izuku Midoriya, 15, nervous and always writing; Katsuki Bakugo, 16, first on the practical; Ayumi Kasahara, 18, from a calligraphy family in Kofu; Wataru Ogawa, 19, a rower from Sendai; Nanami Isogai, 18, from a fishing town on the Sea of Japan.

entries.title: The UA staff
entries.content: Shota Aizawa, 32, is 1-A's homeroom teacher and the hero Eraserhead. Hizashi Yamada, 32, teaches English and is the hero Present Mic. Chiyo Shuzenji, 72, is Recovery Girl, the school nurse. All Might, 55, the Symbol of Peace, teaches Foundational Hero Studies. The principal is rarely seen outside his office.

entries.title: Shota Aizawa
entries.content: Aizawa is an underground hero who avoids cameras and erases a Quirk by looking at it. He has sent home whole classes he judged would not survive the job, and he tells first-years so on their first day. He sleeps wherever he waits and does not raise his voice. He will not say what he thinks happened to the back door.

entries.title: The Commission's inspection
entries.content: The Hero Public Safety Commission licenses every hero and inspects every school that trains them. Since Hosu it can close any dorm it judges unsafe and send the students home to wait out the term. It inspects Heights Alliance this Friday. Its officers ask few questions and write everything down.

entries.title: The Hosu attack
entries.content: Three weeks ago League members broke into a hero agency in Hosu at night, with engineered creatures called Nomu and a flood in the service tunnels. Three pros were badly hurt and two civilians died. The League left the way it came. The Commission has not said how anyone got through a locked agency door.

entries.title: The League of Villains
entries.content: The League of Villains is a loose network that calls hero licensing a cage. Its members are quirked and quirkless alike, and its leaders stay out of sight. It strikes in waves and then vanishes for months. It wants the hero system broken, the Symbol of Peace brought down, and first-years who will listen to an offer.

entries.title: Names
entries.content: Most people here have Japanese names, written given name first: Izuku Midoriya, Ayumi Kasahara, Hatsue Dobashi. Others you will hear: Kenta, Sayuri, Tsubasa, Michiru. A licensed hero takes a hero name, often in English: Eraserhead, Present Mic. Shops take the name of the family that runs them.

entries.title: Shiomi Street
entries.content: Shiomi Street runs downhill from the back of Musutafu station under a covered roof: family shops, a bathhouse, a hardware store, and Dobashi Noodles on the corner, where Hatsue Dobashi, 34, quirkless, feeds first-years cheaply. Agencies patrol the main roads and rarely walk it. Its shutters are mostly down by seven.

entries.title: All Might
entries.content: All Might, 55, has been the number one hero for thirty years and is called the Symbol of Peace; crime fell wherever he stood. About five years ago he began to appear less, and no agency ever said why. This spring he started teaching at UA. Shops on Shiomi Street still keep his poster by the register.

entries.title: Quirks in brief
entries.content: The first Quirks appeared nearly two hundred years ago, and the old order almost broke under them. Heroes became a licensed trade about a hundred and fifty years ago. All Might became number one thirty years ago, and crime fell for a generation. The League struck its first agency four years ago; Hosu, three weeks ago, was its worst.

entries.title: Nomu
entries.content: Nomu are the League's engineered creatures, made by surgery from stolen Quirks. They are huge, fast and hard to hurt, they do not speak, and they cannot be reasoned with. Two appeared in the Hosu footage. Agencies treat any sighting as a full emergency, and nobody has said where they are made.

entries.title: Heteromorphs and the quirkless
entries.content: Some Quirks shape the body itself: scales, extra arms, an animal's head. People with them are called heteromorphs, and some streets still stare. About one person in five has no Quirk at all; they are called quirkless, a plain word in some mouths and an insult in others. Few quirkless people are licensed heroes.

entries.title: The entrance exam
entries.content: UA's entrance exam is a written paper and a practical in a mock city full of robots. The practical scores each applicant for robots stopped and, without telling them, for people helped. Most applicants fail. This spring Katsuki Bakugo came first on the practical, and Izuku Midoriya took the top rescue score.

entries.title: Healing and Recovery Girl
entries.content: Healing Quirks are rare. Recovery Girl's kiss speeds a body's own mending, and the patient pays for it in stamina: a big heal means sleeping through the afternoon, and too many in a week leave a person weak. She will not keep healing the same reckless injury. Ordinary injuries mend with rest. The infirmary is open day and night.

entries.title: Hero licenses and rankings
entries.content: A provisional license lets a student work under a licensed pro; a full one lets a hero work alone and be paid. The Commission revokes licenses after reckless fights. Pros are ranked each year on rescues, arrests and public votes, and the top ten are on television most weeks. A ranking climbs slowly and falls overnight.

entries.title: Hero agencies
entries.content: Hero agencies are private firms of licensed pros who patrol for city and Commission contracts. They compete on rankings and rescues, keep their own uniforms, and sign promising first-years for internships as early as they can. Agency heads sit on the Commission's review board, which judges every serious incident.

entries.title: Support companies
entries.content: Support companies build hero costumes, gauntlets, capture tools and the gear that keeps a Quirk safe to use. The biggest sit in Musutafu's glass district and sell to agencies by the year. Their designs are guarded like secrets, and it is said that a few engineers sell prototypes out the back door.

world.vibe: Bright on the surface and tired underneath, with bad news said flat. Teachers set drills instead of saying they are afraid, and students talk about their Quirks when they mean themselves.

opening.note: Staged. Beat one: the ground-floor corridor of Heights Alliance at twenty to seven on the first morning, the back door burned open and the rest of the building asleep. Shota Aizawa speaks first. He wants a plain account of where the player was at four and what they heard, and he wants it before anyone else comes down. He is flat, not cruel: a straight answer gets one more question and then a nod. He does not mention Friday, his report, or what he suspects. Beat two: at a quarter to seven Wataru Ogawa comes down in rowing kit, sees the door, and says far too quickly that he slept through the night, though nobody asked. Aizawa sends both to breakfast and leaves. At seven Hizashi Yamada's voice fills the hall speaker and calls the first-years to the common room, where he announces, loudly, that the Hero Public Safety Commission inspects Heights Alliance on Friday. Katsuki Bakugo stands at the back with his hands in his pockets and does not look toward the corridor. Beat three: by the third turn the player has three people wanting something from them before the nine o'clock assessment on Ground Gamma. Aizawa wants anything anyone noticed. Wataru wants the stairs forgotten. Izuku Midoriya, notebook open, wants to know what the player's Quirk does, because his page on them is still blank. All Might is heard and not seen, a cough through the staff office door. Nobody in 1-A knows the player yet. Never say what the player's Quirk is or how their exam went.

cast.name: All Might
cast.role: The Symbol of Peace, number one in the hero rankings for thirty years and now a teacher of Foundational Hero Studies at UA; this week he wants Class 1-A to see a hero they can still trust after Hosu.
cast.look: huge in public, with a wide grin and two gold forelocks standing up like horns; in private a gaunt, hollow-cheeked man inside the same suit, eyes sunk in shadow
cast.manner: Booming and theatrical in front of a crowd, hoarse and plain in an empty room. Strikes a pose without meaning to whenever a camera is near. Keeps a handkerchief balled in one fist and puts it away before anyone sees what is on it.
cast.secret: What made him All Might is nearly gone. He can hold his great form for about three hours a day before he shrinks to the thin man he hides, and the cough is blood from a wound five years old. Chiyo Shuzenji and the principal know. He means to teach one more year and step back before the country sees him shrink.

cast.name: Shota Aizawa
cast.role: Homeroom teacher of Class 1-A and the underground hero Eraserhead, who switches off a Quirk by looking at it; this week he wants the burned back door explained before the Commission inspects on Friday.
cast.look: lean and sallow, black hair in a tangle to his shoulders, stubble, red-rimmed eyes, a black jumpsuit and a long grey capture scarf wound twice around his neck
cast.manner: Flat, short sentences with no greeting and no softening. Calls a thing irrational when he means stupid. Climbs into a yellow sleeping bag wherever he has to wait, and listens from inside it with his eyes shut.
cast.secret: He has already written to the principal that the latch failed from a wiring fault, to keep the Commission from closing the dorm on Friday. If anyone learns he wrote it, he loses his license and his class, so he means to find who burned that door before anyone reads the report closely.

cast.name: Hizashi Yamada
cast.role: English teacher, late-night radio host and the loud hero Present Mic; this week he wants the first-years laughing again, and the night at Hosu explained.
cast.look: tall and lanky, blond hair combed straight up a hand's height, tinted orange glasses, a leather jacket, a speaker collar around his neck
cast.manner: Talks in a radio voice, all exclamations, and opens with 'Hey, listeners!' even to an empty room. Conducts with both hands as if a band were behind him. Goes very quiet, and very plain, when a student is frightened.
cast.secret: He kept a recording of the police band from the night of the Hosu attack, which the Commission asked everyone to delete. Near the end a calm voice reads out the agency's back-door code to someone who should not have needed it, and the voice belongs to a Commission liaison he has met at UA. He has not told Shota Aizawa.

cast.name: Chiyo Shuzenji
cast.role: Recovery Girl, UA's nurse, whose kiss speeds a body's own healing at the cost of the patient's stamina; this week she wants fewer students in her beds and a quiet word with Shota Aizawa.
cast.look: tiny and stooped, white hair in a bun under a nurse's cap, round glasses, a white coat, a cane shaped like a syringe, pockets full of wrapped sweets
cast.manner: Brisk and bossy, scolding in every sentence. Hands out a sweet after every treatment and before every lecture. Purses her lips a moment before she heals anyone, and never asks permission twice.
cast.secret: At half past four this morning a first-year came to her window with both palms burned raw and asked her to say nothing. She healed him, wrote the visit down as six o'clock, and has told nobody, because she thinks he has not slept properly since the exam.

cast.name: Izuku Midoriya
cast.role: First-year in Class 1-A, nervous and earnest, whose Quirk breaks his own bones when he uses it; this week he wants a page in his notebook for every Quirk in the class.
cast.look: short and wiry, a mess of dark green hair, freckles, round eyes, scarred fingers, a battered notebook in his blazer pocket and red sneakers
cast.manner: Mutters long runs of analysis under his breath without noticing he is doing it. Bows too often and talks in breathless run-on sentences when he is excited or scared. Goes still and steady the moment someone is in danger.
cast.secret: His Quirk is not his own. All Might passed it to him: One For All, a power handed from one holder to the next, far too strong for his body yet, so every full use breaks bones. He tells people it came in late and says nothing else, and he would lie to a teacher before he said where it came from.

cast.name: Katsuki Bakugo
cast.role: First-year in Class 1-A who came first on the practical exam, with a Quirk that sets off blasts from the sweat of his palms; this week he wants to be ahead of everyone in the class by Friday.
cast.look: ash-blond hair in hard spikes, red eyes in a fixed glare, a blazer worn open with the tie pulled loose, hands kept in his pockets
cast.manner: Loud and blunt, in orders rather than requests. Pops a small crackle from one palm when he has stopped listening. Walks fast and never waits for anyone to catch up.
cast.secret: He burned out the back-door latch at four this morning to train alone on Ground Beta, because he lost the exam's top rescue score to Izuku Midoriya, whom he had written off as quirkless, and he has not slept properly since. Recovery Girl healed his palms at half past four. He would let the staff blame the League before he said why he was out.

cast.name: Ayumi Kasahara
cast.role: First-year in Class 1-A whose Quirk, Ink Thread, spins ink into lines strong enough to hold a falling person; from a calligraphy family in Kofu, she wants to be a rescue hero and is short of money.
cast.look: square-shouldered and quick, short black hair with one ink-dyed streak, fingertips stained dark, a brown blazer worn soft at the elbows
cast.manner: Polite and very formal, every sentence complete, until she is angry and drops all of it at once. Corrects other people's handwriting without being asked. Rolls a dry brush between her palms while she listens.
cast.secret: She sends most of a part-time wage home to keep her family's studio open. Last week a man at the Dobashi Noodles counter offered to clear the studio's debt if she would tell him which first-years go out alone. She has not said yes. She has not said no.

cast.name: Wataru Ogawa
cast.role: First-year in Class 1-A whose Quirk, Gale Palms, throws a burst of air hard enough to shove a car sideways; a rower from Sendai, he wants to stop being the one who gets carried out.
cast.look: broad and tall, a thick neck, hair cropped the color of wet sand, a cracked scar across his left palm, a rowing club jacket with the sleeves cut off
cast.manner: Loud, cheerful and eager to be liked, and laughs at the start of his own sentences. Rolls his shoulders back like a rower on the start line whenever he is nervous, and talks faster the more nervous he gets.
cast.secret: He wakes at four every day, a habit from the rowing club, and this morning from his window he saw Katsuki Bakugo go out the back door. He has decided he saw nothing: Bakugo frightens him, and after being carried unconscious out of the exam he will not be the first-year who causes trouble.

cast.name: Nanami Isogai
cast.role: First-year in Class 1-A whose Quirk, Tidewell, draws water up through stone and holds it there; from a fishing town on the Sea of Japan, she wants to work water rescue and does not trust the city.
cast.look: lean, with pale freckles, a long braid dyed grey over one shoulder, a windbreaker that always looks damp, salt dried white at the hem of her jeans
cast.manner: Speaks softly in her town's dialect and drops it the moment a teacher is near. Ties and unties the end of her braid while she thinks. Laughs out loud, suddenly, at things nobody else finds funny.
cast.secret: She was in Hosu the night of the attack and held a flooded service tunnel open long enough for nine people to climb out, an unlicensed use of a Quirk that would end her place at UA. Only Hatsue Dobashi knows, because Nanami came into the shop the next morning and Hatsue stitched the cut on her arm.

cast.name: Hatsue Dobashi
cast.role: Owner of Dobashi Noodles on Shiomi Street, below Musutafu station; quirkless, she feeds half the first-years cheaply and hears what the agencies never ask about.
cast.look: compact and strong-armed, a white headband over bobbed black hair, flour to the elbows, a faded apron with a carp stitched by hand on the pocket
cast.manner: Dry and unhurried. Passes on what she has heard with the day and the stool it was said on, and keeps her own opinion to herself unless she is asked three times.
cast.secret: For two weeks a man in a grey work jacket has eaten at her counter every evening and asked which first-years come in alone. She has photographed him twice through the steam with her phone and told no agency, because no agency has ever asked her anything.

systems.label: Standing at UA
systems.meaning: How the staff rate you as a future hero, from drills, grades and what they write in your file. High standing opens internships; low standing puts your file on the principal's desk.
systems.change: Up with drills passed, rescues done well and honest reports. Down with failed assessments, reckless Quirk use, curfew broken and lies the staff catch.

systems.label: Public Eye
systems.meaning: How well the city knows your face, and how kindly. A first-year people like gets agency offers and a crowd; one they doubt gets every mistake replayed.
systems.change: Up with rescues people film and good words in the news. Down when footage of something reckless spreads or a rumor reaches the feeds.

systems.label: Quirk Control
systems.meaning: How well you hold your Quirk under pressure: at full strength without hurting yourself, or down to a whisper when that is what the moment needs.
systems.change: Up with drills, careful use in real danger and lessons from the staff. Down with overuse, blackouts and fights where the power ran away with you.

systems.label: The back door
systems.start: Burned open at four on the first morning. Nobody has said by whom.
systems.meaning: What you know about who burned open the Heights Alliance back door, and why.
systems.change: Grows with each thing you learn: who was awake, who is lying, what the staff have written. It matters most before Friday's inspection.

npcSystems.label: Trust
npcSystems.meaning: How far this person trusts you with what they know.
npcSystems.change: Up when you keep a confidence, do what you said you would, or stand beside them when it costs you. Down when you repeat what they told you, lie to them, or let them take blame that was yours.

style.art: Anime cel shading with bold ink lines, primary red, blue and yellow against grey harbor haze: UA's white towers and steel dorm, steamy shopping streets, students in hero costume beside commuters in coats.

heroes.name: Rin Takeda
heroes.description: A first-year from Kanazawa whose Quirk bends light into a short, hot beam, here on her second try at the exam and done with waiting.
heroes.look: Compact and quick, shoulder-length black hair in a low tail, a secondhand jacket with a patch over its old crest, a ring of burn scars on her left wrist.
heroes.background: Rin's older brother was a licensed hero until a bad fight ended his career, and she has heard his leg brace on the stairs at home ever since. She failed the UA exam once, worked a year grinding lenses in a Kanazawa optician's back room, and passed this spring. She has never told her family how close she came to quitting.
heroes.carries: A repair kit for her beam lens, her brother's old agency ID badge, and a license form she has not filled in.

heroes.name: Oren Guerrero
heroes.description: A welder from Hamamatsu whose Quirk pulls loose metal to his hands, and who feels every key and coin in a crowded train.
heroes.look: Tall and loose-limbed, dark curls cut short at the sides, a denim jacket covered in pin badges, silver rings on every finger, old burns along both forearms.
heroes.background: Oren worked two years on the welding line in his father's shop in Hamamatsu after his father hurt his back, catching dropped tools before they landed. A pro who brought in her armor to be patched told him his Quirk was wasted on a shop floor. He sat the exam at twenty with his father's blessing and most of his savings.
heroes.carries: A magnet clip on a leather cord, a welding glove, and a roll of costume patterns pinned with welding clips.

heroes.name: Linh Ngo
heroes.description: A former agency dispatcher from Kobe whose Quirk leaves an echo of their footsteps that walks on for two seconds after they stop.
heroes.look: Narrow and pale, short hair dyed dark plum, an oversized hoodie with the sleeves rolled, a silver ear cuff, a groove in their hair where a headset sat for years.
heroes.background: Linh spent three years on the radio desk of a small agency in Kobe, sending heroes to calls they could only hear. The agency folded after a raid went wrong, and Linh decided they were done listening from a chair. UA was the one school that answered their application.
heroes.carries: A worn headset with a cut cord, a tin of cough drops, and a cheap phone with a cracked screen.
